entries.text: My cousin fenced a candlestick from {name} once. Swears it walked back home on its own
The thieves took the wrong thing. The real treasure's still somewhere near {its:feature}
They say the thief who hit that {l:function} still drinks here, bold as brass
Folk say what was stolen from {name} was a fake all along, and the owners knew
Never buy anything that smells of {name}. Stolen goods from there come back to haunt you
The fire-priests want back what was stolen from {name}, and they aren't asking nicely
A pirate in the harbour's selling bits of {name} by the pound. Cheap, too. Too cheap
Spend a night in {name} and you wake a year older. My uncle did, or so my uncle claims
Don't take so much as a pebble from {name}. The curse follows the pebble
The curse on that {l:function}? Started with one unpaid bill, my gran says
Every owner of {name} dies on a feast day. Every single one, I swear it
They say a kiss on the doorstep of {name} breaks the curse. Nobody's volunteered
They buried the last owner of {name} face down, to be safe
Never thank anyone inside {name}. The fey count thanks as payment, and the curse collects
Whoever built {name} made a deal. Now something's come to collect, and it doesn't take coin
My gran says {its:feature} was the price of the pact. Or the down payment
Sign nothing inside {name}. Not the guestbook, not a bar tab, nothing
The contract for that {l:function} is written on skin, they say. Whose skin, nobody says
They say the debt passes to whoever sleeps in {name} last. So nobody sleeps there
A devil drinks in the back room of {name} every tenth night, holding a sheaf of paper
Everyone knows who sold out {name}. Nobody says it, because they own half the town
The traitor still leaves flowers at {name} every year. Guilt, or checking it stays dead
My old sergeant was there the night {name} fell. Says the gates were opened from inside
They say the founder left a letter naming the traitor. It's somewhere near {its:feature}
That {l:function} was sold out for thirty silver and a title. The title's still in use
The clans have a hunt-mark out for whoever wronged {name}. They've not caught them yet
My grandfather found {name} once, drunk as a lord. Sober, never again
Maps lie about {name}. You follow the moths, my mother says
Three expeditions went looking for that {l:function}. One came back, and won't talk
They say {name} only shows itself to the desperate. Good thing I'm desperate
Sailors swear the lights of {name} still show on foggy nights, far out at sea
A Sigil cabbie claims to know a door that opens straight into {name}. For a fee
{name} breathes. Lean on the walls at night and you'll feel it
Something under {name} woke up, and it's been asking for someone by name
Doors in {name} lock themselves now. Unlock themselves too, when it wants company
My cousin swears {its:feature} turned to watch the road last market day
The dead of {name} vote in the town elections now. Always the same way
Don't dig near {name}. It's not keeping folk out, it's keeping something in
The old keeper of {name} told me what's under it, then asked me to forget
They say if {name} ever falls, the river runs backwards, and worse follows
{its:feature} isn't decoration, friend. It's a lock
The drow pay good coin for news of {name}. Makes you wonder what's in the cellar
When the snow on the roof of {name} melts, run. That's all my gran ever said
Angels were seen on the roof of {name} last solstice. Guarding it, or waiting for it to fall
Half the fences in the city have been offered a piece of {name}. None of them took it
The watch knows who robbed that {l:function}. The watch got paid, too
My dog won't walk past {name}. Smartest thing in this village, that dog
A priest went in to lift the curse on that {l:function}. Came out and joined a different faith
Every year on the same night, a stranger knocks at {name} with a ledger. Nobody answers anymore
They say the deal that saved {name} has a clause about the founder's heirs. Never met an heir who lived long
Ask about the night {name} fell, and watch who leaves the room first
The one who sold out {name} is buried under a fancy stone. Empty grave, if you ask me
A tinker sold me directions to {name}. Different directions every time I asked
You don't find {name}. It finds you, usually when you're lost and scared
Walk past {name} after dark and it creaks your name. Mine, anyway
The cats all left the streets around {name}. Cats know when a house wakes up
Every hundred years, something knocks from under {name}. It's been ninety-nine, my gran says
The warding marks on that {l:function} get repainted every spring, and nobody knows who does it
My aunt read tea leaves over {name} and they spelled a date. Next month's date
Some hooded lot keep measuring the doorway of {name}. For a coffin or a crown, I reckon
A seer told my ma {name} will be the last thing standing. Last thing standing after what, eh
No fortune-teller in the district will read cards about {name}. That's a sign in itself
They say the chosen one will walk out of {name} carrying fire. Probably a torch
The prophecy about that {l:function} is real, my priest says. The ending just keeps changing
The academy's forbidden shelf has a whole book on {name}. The last page is blank
A bard sang about {name} once, and the ending came true word for word
